display.purpose: The single largest type in the product: the first-viewport status sentence. Vermilion <em> on the number, max 46ch, text-wrap: balance.

headline.purpose: App title, plate titles, empty-state headings, boot wordmark. Bodoni italic 26px.

title.purpose: Agent names in the catalogue, modal headings, card titles. Names only, never data.

body.purpose: Rows, descriptions, help. Archivo 12-13px, prose capped at 44-72ch.

label.purpose: Small-caps vermilion annotation: section heads, field labels, column heads, badges, chips.

readout.purpose: Every number and path. JetBrains Mono with tabular-nums; body disables tnum so this stays a signal.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Plates, prompt cards, diff panes. Just enough that the plate sits on paper instead of being cut out of it.

shadows.name: pop
shadows.purpose: Slash-command menu and the office viewscreen.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: The only genuinely lifted surface in the system.

shadows.name: screen
shadows.purpose: Terminals are recessed, not raised. Anything on --void gets no shadow.

shadows.name: card-day
shadows.purpose: Paper edition re-tint: ink on paper does not throw a neutral shadow.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: Modal backdrop, paired with a 3px backdrop blur.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for entrances and state settles.

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: Hover lift and release; wrapped in @supports with the ease-out curve as fallback.

motion.name: t-release
motion.purpose: Transform release on the spring curve.

motion.name: t-ui
motion.purpose: Background, border, shadow; disclosure and menu entrances.

motion.name: t-pane
motion.purpose: plate-in — the one authored entrance, on main > *.

motion.name: t-theme
motion.purpose: Plate change; applied by a temporary .theme-shifting class and removed after, so hover never feels laggy.

motion.name: sidereal
motion.purpose: Starfield drift on .app::before — the world's own continuous motion.

motion.name: reticle-turn
motion.purpose: The observation reticle around the focused star.

motion.name: star-pulse
motion.purpose: Working and waiting status stars; preserved (slowed to 2.6s) under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview:
Project state is not a dashboard; it is an astronomical plate. Agents are stars, their token weight is magnitude (dot diameter), their status is colour and form, and a delegation is a real constellation line drawn between two of them. Everything the plate draws comes from live data — the mapping is documented in src/components/Sky.tsx and there is no decorative geometry anywhere in it. The system deliberately refuses the category default it grew out of: card grid, status pills, sparkline row.

The surface is print, not glass. Ground is night ink carrying a real grain tile and a 128px graticule; plates are flat ink fields with hairline frames and a 2px corner; type is engraved Bodoni italic for names and the status sentence, Archivo for the interface, JetBrains Mono for every number. There is exactly one accent — vermilion — and it behaves like annotation ink written on the plate rather than a brand fill. Density is high (this is a tool for someone running eight agents at once) but the first viewport spends its space on a single sentence, because the product's first job is to report state, not to report data.

Three editions exist, and each answers a real observing condition rather than a colour preference: Gece (night ink, the default for a panel left open for hours), Kırmızı Fener (observer's red lamp — no blue at all, so status separates by brightness and form), Gündüz (printed plate on paper for a lit room; print does not glow, so the halo token goes to 0). Interface language is Turkish throughout.
keyCharacteristics: Data-true diagram: magnitude = tokens, colour + form = status, line = delegation
One accent (vermilion), used as annotation, never as a large fill
Hairline separation (1px) and space instead of cards and shadows
Print materials: grain tile, graticule, engraved italic; no glass, no gradients-as-decor
Contrast is measured by a script, not judged by eye
One authored entrance animation for the whole app

rules.name: The Channel Rule
rules.body: Every colour is stored as an R G B channel triple (--accent-rgb: 255 77 46) and consumed as rgb(var(--accent-rgb) / a). Raw colour literals are forbidden in component CSS; the only exception is pure-black shadow. A theme that cannot be expressed as channel overrides is not a theme.

rules.name: The Twice-Derived Rule
rules.body: Named colours (--fg, --hud, --nominal…) are declared in a separate block whose selector is ':root, [data-theme]' — never ':root' alone. Custom properties inherit as computed values, so a ':root'-only derivation resolves once at the root and cannot be re-derived by a nested container. The theme picker's miniature preview is exactly such a container; before the split, all three previews rendered identically.

rules.name: The Measured Contrast Rule
rules.body: Contrast is never judged by eye. 'node scripts/contrast.mjs' measures every role against both the plate surface and the outer ground and exits 1 on any failure: fg ≥ 7, muted ≥ 4.5, dim / accent / ok / warn / err / aux ≥ 3. All three editions currently pass. A new plate is not done until the script is green.

rules.name: The Annotation Rule
rules.body: Vermilion annotates, it does not upholster. It appears as 1px rules, 5px bullets, 10px labels, a focus ring, and one filled stamp per view. Wide vermilion fills belong to no surface in this system.

rules.name: The Engraved Name Rule
rules.body: Bodoni italic is reserved for names and one sentence: titles, agent names, the status line. A number, a path, or a status word never gets the display face.

rules.name: The Coordinate Rule
rules.body: Anything measured is mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, right-aligned in tabular columns. body explicitly disables tnum so proportional text stays proportional — the tabular figure is a deliberate signal, not a global default.

rules.name: The Shared Ruler Rule
rules.body: A tabular surface declares its grid-template-columns once and both the header row and every data row use it (.cat-head, .cat-row). If a column is dropped at a breakpoint, it is dropped from the shared declaration — never by patching one side.

rules.name: The Card-Grid Refusal
rules.body: Repeating entities are hairline rows on a shared ruler with an expanding detail, not a grid of equally weighted boxes. The agent catalogue was a nine-card grid; it became nine rows because nine identical cards say nothing about which agent matters.

rules.name: The Recessed Screen Rule
rules.body: Anything that is a screen — terminal, diff body, input, code block — sits on void with no shadow. Anything that is a page sits on a plate with the card shadow. Nothing sits on both.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: One weight (1px), one radius (2px). If a boundary needs more emphasis, brighten it (--edge → --edge-lit → --hud); never thicken it.

rules.name: The Terminated Rule
rules.body: A section rule is a 1px vermilion line ending in a small filled dot, not a plain divider. It reads as a plate annotation and it is what marks a heading as a heading (.rule, .eph-mod-head::after, .panel h3::after).

dos: Do define every new colour as an R G B channel token and consume it as rgb(var(--x-rgb) / a).
Do add derived colour names to the ':root, [data-theme]' block, never to ':root' alone — otherwise the theme-preview swatch silently stops working.
Do run 'node scripts/contrast.mjs' before accepting any palette change; all thresholds must pass against both --surface-rgb and --bg-rgb.
Do register a new plate in exactly two places: a token-only block in themes.css and one row in themes.ts.

Do put every transition for interactive elements in the motion layer's shared selector list near the top of index.css. A transition written inside a component rule lands after the motion layer and overrides it, and the interaction snaps.
Do use animation-fill-mode: backwards. 'both' permanently applies transform: none at the end and kills hover motion entirely.
Do keep spacing on the --s1…--s6 scale and numbers in mono with tabular figures.
Do encode status with colour AND form (ring, hollow, fill), so the red-lamp plate and colour-blind readers still separate the states.
Do keep interface copy in Turkish, including empty states and aria labels.
donts: Don't write a raw colour literal in component CSS. The only exception is black in a shadow — and the day plate proves even that gets re-tinted per edition.
Don't write selectors in themes.css. A plate overrides tokens; if a plate needs a new structural behaviour, the token for it goes in index.css first.

Don't add a second entrance animation. plate-in on 'main > *' is the only authored entrance in the app; the world's continuous motion is sidereal drift, reticle turn and star pulse. Genuine appearance events — modal, slash menu, permission banner, a new transcript line, a disclosure panel — are separate and allowed; a section that merely re-renders is not one of them.

Don't disable feedback under prefers-reduced-motion. Positional motion is removed and durations are cut, but the working/waiting pulses and the CLI spinner are explicitly preserved — with them gone, 'is it running?' has no visual answer.
Don't thicken a border or round a corner for emphasis. Brighten the edge instead.
Don't introduce glass, ring shadows, or glow on plate chrome. --glass-blur is 0 and the day plate sets --glow-a: 0; anything that reads as luminous will look broken on paper.
Don't let the CLI skin palettes escape .terminal[data-cli], and don't add plate tokens to them — they are fixed-palette islands by design.
Don't draw geometry the data does not support. No invented coordinates, no unlabelled grid, no decorative constellation. Every mark on the sky maps to a field.
Don't rebuild a repeating list as a card grid.
